mood.summary: Fear is still running high. On Nov 5 the S&P 500 fell 4.4% and the Nasdaq slid into a correction, the worst day since April 2025, on worries that election results will slow AI and data-centre spending. The Fear & Greed index sits in Extreme Fear at 20, and bearish individual investors outnumber bulls by about 14 points. Stocks are bouncing on Nov 6 after a strong jobs report (165,000 jobs vs about 60,000 expected), but that also firmed bets on a December Fed rate hike.

trending.note: Board as of Thursday 4:06 PM ET; prices are the 2026-11-19 close. Why-it's-trending notes summarize the Stocktwits stream and the news it links to.

items.name: Anthropic
items.about: Anthropic develops the Claude family of AI models and sells access to them to businesses and consumers.
items.why: Anthropic began trading on Nasdaq today after pricing its 825 million share IPO at $83, above the $70-78 marketed range, which values it at well over $1 trillion. Shares opened near $112.97 and faded to close around $96.97, about 17% above the IPO price but roughly 14% below the open.

items.name: Nebius Group
items.about: Nebius rents GPU cloud capacity and AI infrastructure to companies that train and run AI models.
items.why: Shares fell about 9.4% as AI infrastructure names sold off again. The stock is still under pressure from its Nov 12 Q3 report: revenue of $980.8M beat estimates, but Nebius trimmed the top of its 2026 guidance, pushed its $7B run-rate target to February 2027 because of data-center delays, and raised spending plans. It fell 16.8% that day.

items.name: GameStop
items.about: GameStop sells video games, consoles and collectibles, and holds a stake of about 9.8% in eBay.
items.why: Posts say GME topped today's bullish options-flow lists, with about $50.7M of call premium across roughly 497,000 contracts. No company news was found today. The long-running $125-per-share eBay bid and the eBay stake remain the main background story.

items.name: Invesco QQQ Trust
items.about: QQQ tracks the Nasdaq-100, the largest non-financial companies listed on Nasdaq.
items.why: The Nasdaq-100 fund fell about 2.2% as a weeks-long selloff in AI and chip stocks resumed. Nvidia slid after its earnings, AMD lost 7.7%, and the Anthropic debut failed to lift the group. Posts point to the S&P 500 testing its 200-day average and to worries about the midterm results.

items.name: Advanced Micro Devices
items.about: AMD designs CPUs, GPUs and AI accelerators for PCs, data centers and gaming.
items.why: AMD dropped about 7.7%, adding to a steep November slide. The stock fell about 17% on Nov 5 in a post-midterm chip selloff, 8.8% on Nov 13 and 5.6% on Nov 16, when it closed its World Labs purchase. As of Nov 16 it was already about 18% below its Oct 6 high of $649.

items.name: Alibaba Group
items.about: Alibaba runs China's largest e-commerce marketplaces and the Alibaba Cloud AI and computing business.
items.why: Alibaba slipped only about 1.3%, holding up better than US tech. Posts are circulating a House Foreign Affairs Committee release of AI chip export-license data. Posts say it shows U.S. approval of more than 879,000 Nvidia and AMD chips for China, with Alibaba among the buyers. Quarterly results are expected in late November.

items.name: IREN Limited
items.about: IREN operates data centers that it is converting from bitcoin mining to renting out GPU capacity for AI.
items.why: IREN fell about 5.5% as neocloud peers such as Nebius and CoreWeave sold off. In October it was reported to have signed a multi-year AI cloud deal with Anthropic, which was never confirmed. Posts say holders had hoped the Anthropic IPO would lift it.

items.name: Savara
items.about: Savara develops MOLBREEVI, an inhaled therapy for the rare lung disease autoimmune pulmonary alveolar proteinosis.
items.why: Shares rose about 10.4% ahead of an FDA decision on MOLBREEVI due Nov 22, 2026. The drug is under priority review with no advisory committee planned. Savara says approval would unlock up to $150M in non-dilutive financing, and UK and EU decisions are expected in Q4 2026 and Q1 2027.

items.name: Strategy
items.about: Strategy, formerly MicroStrategy, is a software company that holds a very large bitcoin treasury funded by stock and debt sales.
items.why: Strategy fell about 4.7% as bitcoin stayed weak near three-month lows around $64,000-65,000, alongside the tech selloff. MSCI has also said it will drop Strategy from its global indexes, including the MSCI USA Index, after the close on Nov 30, which could force index funds to sell.

items.name: Fundrise Innovation Fund
items.about: VCX is a NYSE-listed closed-end fund that owns stakes in private tech companies such as Anthropic, Databricks and SpaceX.
items.why: VCX fell about 19.6% on the day Anthropic, its largest holding at about 21% of assets, started trading publicly. Investors can now buy Anthropic directly instead of through the fund. The price is now below VCX's last reported NAV of $21.70, and posts say the discount tops 40% on newer estimates.

items.name: NVIDIA
items.about: NVIDIA designs the GPUs and networking systems that power most AI data centers.
items.why: Nvidia fell about 3.3% the day after earnings, even though it beat estimates. Q3 FY27 revenue was $115.8B, up 103% and ahead of the roughly $109B expected, and adjusted EPS was $2.68 against $2.48 expected. It guided Q4 to $130B, excluding China. This was its first report since Jensen Huang's exit, and the stock is down sharply this year.

items.name: Insmed
items.about: Insmed sells treatments for serious lung diseases, including Brinsupri for bronchiectasis and Arikayce.
items.why: Insmed jumped about 20.6%. Posts say Bloomberg reported that Sanofi is weighing a takeover, but neither company has confirmed. Posts also cite a Jefferies note saying Sanofi could afford a deal of about €31B at a 30% premium, plus heavy call buying of about $23.8M. Insmed added former Sanofi CEO Paul Hudson to its board in October.

items.name: SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF
items.about: DIA tracks the 30 blue-chip stocks of the Dow Jones Industrial Average.
items.why: The Dow fund fell about 2.2%, extending a rough week after a 1.6% Dow drop on Nov 17. Selling spread from AI and chip stocks into the broad market. Posts blame the midterm results and the timing of Nvidia's earnings next to the Anthropic IPO.

items.name: VanEck Semiconductor ETF
items.about: SMH holds the largest US-listed semiconductor companies, led by Nvidia, TSMC and Broadcom.
items.why: The chip fund fell about 2.6% as its biggest holdings sold off: AMD lost 7.7% and Nvidia 3.3% after earnings. Chipmakers have been hit repeatedly this month by doubts about AI spending, and the sector gauge fell 4.5% earlier this week. Posts say SMH is still up about 25% this year.

items.name: SoFi Technologies
items.about: SoFi is an online bank offering loans, deposits, investing and a financial technology platform.
items.why: SoFi fell about 4.2%, below its October low of about $13.86, setting a new 52-week low. The stock is down more than 40% this year and fell with other fintechs today, including Klarna. Posts cite strong Q3 results, with revenue up 44% to $1.4B, but that has not stopped the slide.

items.name: Baidu
items.about: Baidu runs China's largest search engine and is building AI cloud, chip (Kunlunxin) and robotaxi businesses.
items.why: Baidu fell about 4.2%, extending its losses since its Nov 16 Q3 report. Revenue slipped 1% to RMB30.8B as ad sales dropped 22%, and adjusted EPS per ADS fell to RMB6.78. AI cloud infrastructure revenue rose 94% to RMB8.2B, but the Kunlunxin chip unit's listing may slip to next year.

items.name: Intuit
items.about: Intuit makes TurboTax, QuickBooks, Credit Karma and Mailchimp software for consumers and small businesses.
items.why: Intuit fell about 13% after hours after its fiscal Q1 update. Posts say Q2 guidance was adjusted EPS of $3.17-3.22 against $3.98 expected and revenue of about $4.93-4.95B against $5.11B. Posts also say full-year FY27 revenue guidance was cut to $23.08-23.37B and mention a Mailchimp sale; these figures were not independently confirmed.

items.name: Klarna Group
items.about: Klarna is a buy now, pay later payments company that also offers banking and shopping services.
items.why: Klarna dropped about 12.3%, extending its losses after its Nov 17 Q3 report. Revenue rose 12% to about $1.01B and gross merchandise volume rose 10% to $36.1B, but it lost $65M, or $0.19 per share against $0.15 expected. It kept its full-year outlook. No other news was found today; the stock fell with other fintechs.

items.name: Figma
items.about: Figma makes browser-based tools that teams use to design and prototype apps and websites.
items.why: Figma fell about 6%, below its earlier low of about $16.60, setting a new 52-week low. The stock is down more than 80% from its post-IPO highs because of worries about AI design tools from rivals such as Google and ongoing insider selling. Posts compare its fall after the IPO hype to Anthropic's debut.

items.name: Abivax
items.about: Abivax is a French biotech developing obefazimod, a once-daily pill for ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease.
items.why: Abivax slipped about 3.8% during a weak week for biotech. It is still recovering from June's Phase 3 maintenance data, when cancer cases in 9 of 580 patients sent shares down as much as 44% in one day. An FDA filing is planned for late 2026. Posts flag speculative call buying at the $86 and $120 strikes.
